scenicChapters.title: Top of the Rockies Scenic Byway
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 3687 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance. Cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Top of the Rockies Scenic Byway
scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 35 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.

facts.v: Top of the Rockies Scenic Byway

scenicChapters.title: Top of the Rockies Scenic Byway
scenicChapters.narrative: 3186 m come off over 46 km at around 9.5%. The road gives back what the climb took, faster than it took it — brakes early, eyes far ahead. A descent this long asks more of concentration than of pace.

top-of-the-rockies-scenic-byway.story: From Aspen it runs 171 km to Minturn; allow about 2 h 25 of riding. It goes by way of Independence Pass, Twin Lakes, Leadville and Tennessee Pass. The highest point is about 3,700 m. Independence Pass Colorado is subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.
